title: Mulgore
body: Mulgore is the homeland of the tauren, a sheltered valley of golden grass ringed by mountains west of the Barrens. The tauren wandered as nomads, harried by the centaur, until Cairne Bloodhoof, aided by Thrall's orcs, drove the centaur back and claimed the plains, raising Thunder Bluff in the north as a refuge for every tribe. Their peace is not complete: quilboar raid from their ravine, gnolls poach the wildlife, and goblins of the Venture Company have poisoned the sacred wells.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Mulgore (Warcraft III section: Cairne led the tauren to Mulgore with Thrall's help, centaur driven back, Thunder Bluff founded as a refuge for every tribe, tribes united; enemies of the WoW era)

title: Camp Narache
body: Camp Narache, on the northern edge of Red Cloud Mesa high above southern Mulgore, is where young tauren take their first steps toward adulthood. Chief Hawkwind presides and warns every eager newcomer that eagerness is no substitute for wisdom. From here the young set out on the Rites of the Earthmother, trials of strength, vision and wisdom that earn the respect of the elders, and young shaman drink their first sapta at the shrine beneath Kodo Rock.

title: Brambleblade Ravine
body: East of Camp Narache, Brambleblade Ravine is the home of the Bristleback quilboar, who wage a stubborn war on the tauren from a makeshift village. Their raiders ambush hunting parties and steal from the camp by night, their battleboars are trained to savagery, and at the back of the ravine their leader, Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle, keeps his hut.

parts.body: A dirt-stained map from the ravine holds plans drawn up by the Bristleback warchief for an extended siege of Camp Narache: the quilboar mean far more than raids.

title: Bloodhoof Village
body: Bloodhoof Village, named for the tribe of Cairne Bloodhoof, sits in the heart of Mulgore within the curve of Stonebull Lake, the busiest place on the plains outside Thunder Bluff. Cairne's son Baine is its chief. Here young tauren walking the Rites of the Earthmother drink the Water of the Seers that Zarlman Two-Moons brews before the tribal fire, and follow the vision it shows them across the plains.

title: The Sacred Wells
body: Three sacred wells, named for the Winterhoof, Thunderhorn and Wildmane clans, water the people and beasts of Mulgore. Goblins of the Venture Company have overrun all three and fouled the water with their poisons, and driving them off is not enough: Mull Thunderhorn of Bloodhoof Village must bind the power of the plains' creatures into totems to cleanse each well.

parts.body: When the Wildmane well, last and farthest, ran clean, Mull declared the land healed and prayed that the waters of Mulgore stay clean forever.

title: The Venture Co. Mine
body: Refused mining rights in the tauren homeland, the Venture Company dug anyway, boring a mine into Mulgore's eastern mountains under Supervisor Fizsprocket. The Outrunners, who keep the plains safe, have already burned one of its guarded caravans on the shore of Stonebull Lake, though goblin salvagers keep creeping back to the wreck.

parts.body: Papers from the caravan's crates, approved by the company president Razdunk, press for more ore from Mulgore and promise shredders and a lumber mill besides: the goblins want the plains' timber too.

title: Red Rocks
body: Red Rocks, a formation of red sandstone east of Thunder Bluff, is the most sacred burial ground of the tauren. Only the most valiant lie there: the warriors who founded and defended Thunder Bluff and those who gave their lives for their tribes. Their spirits linger among the stones, and the young who complete the Rites of the Earthmother come here last, to receive their blessing.

parts.body: There the ancestral spirits pass their duty of protection on to the young tauren, who may then enter Thunder Bluff with pride.

title: Baine Bloodhoof
body: Baine is the son of Cairne Bloodhoof and chief of Bloodhoof Village. After the Third War centaur raiders carried him off, and his grieving father lost the will to lead, until the wanderer Rexxar found the centaur camp and brought Baine home. Calm and thoughtful, he holds that the land has been good to the tauren and must be respected, and he sets himself against the gnolls who poach its beasts and the dwarves who hollow its hills.
